newsitem.title: BERMUDA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA OFF TO BAD START VS NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA OFF TO BAD START VS NZ.

text.p: Sri Lanka made a disastrous start to their quest for victory late on the third day of the second cricket test against New Zealand on Sunday.
Sri Lanka's chances of scoring the 326 runs required to win received an immediate setback when opening batsman Sanath Jayasuriya ran himself out while seeking a second run in just the second over.
Worse was to follow in the ninth over when left arm spinner Daniel Vettori bowled Hashan Tillekaratne around his legs before Sri Lanka limped to stumps on 20 for two.

New Zealand were dismissed for 273 in their second innings, holding an overall advantage of 325 with more than two days to play, before Jayasuriya senselessly ran himself out after turning a delivery from Heath Davis behind square leg.

Simon Doull, fielding on the fine leg boundary, ran in quickly and fired a quick and accurate return to wicketkeeper Adam Parore. Jayasuriya chanced his arm and paid the penalty when he was found just short of his ground.
Sri Lanka will resume on Monday with Roshan Mahanama on six and night watchman Chaminda Vaas on nought.
New Zealand's second innings score featured half-centuries to Bryan Young, with 62, captain Stephen Fleming, with 59, and Nathan Astle, 52.
Offspinner Muttiah Muralitharan took three for 62 and young left arm seamer Nuwan Zoysa captured three for 53.
Muralitharan's dismissal of Fleming, who was bowled around his legs, saw the spinner become the first Sri Lankan bowler to take 100 wickets in tests.
